lab_questions.title: Practical SQLite Scenarios
lab_questions.description: Evaluate candidates on their practical SQLite skills, including query optimization, date manipulation, and advanced SQLite features like JSON, FTS5, and Window Functions.

tasks.title: Query Optimization: Slow Email Lookup
tasks.description: A `users` table contains 5 million records. The following query is taking several seconds: `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = 'abc@example.com';`. Identify why the query is slow and write the SQLite statement to optimize this lookup.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='index' AND tbl_name='users' AND name='idx_users_email';

tasks.title: Inventory Sync: Upserting Records
tasks.description: You are syncing inventory data from a third-party API. Given an `inventory` table with `product_id` (PRIMARY KEY) and `quantity`, write an SQLite query to insert a new product (ID 101, Quantity 50) or update its quantity to 50 if the product already exists.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT quantity FROM inventory WHERE product_id = 101;

solution.query.sql: INSERT INTO inventory (product_id, quantity) VALUES (101, 50) ON CONFLICT(product_id) DO UPDATE SET quantity = excluded.quantity;

tasks.title: Analytics: Extracting JSON Data
tasks.description: Your app stores event metadata in an `events` table (id, event_type, payload). The `payload` column contains JSON strings like `{"browser": "Chrome", "os": "Mac"}`. Write a query to find the top 3 most used browsers for 'page_view' events. Return `browser` and `count`.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT json_extract(payload, '$.browser') AS browser, COUNT(*) AS count FROM events WHERE event_type = 'page_view' GROUP BY browser ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 3;

solution.query.sql: SELECT json_extract(payload, '$.browser') AS browser, COUNT(*) AS count FROM events WHERE event_type = 'page_view' GROUP BY browser ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 3;

tasks.title: Reporting: Monthly Signups
tasks.description: Given a `signups` table (id, user_id, signup_date) where `signup_date` is a TEXT column in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' format. Write a query to count the number of signups per month in the year 2023. Output `month` (e.g., '2023-01') and `signup_count`.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', signup_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS signup_count FROM signups WHERE signup_date LIKE '2023-%' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month LIMIT 1;

solution.query.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', signup_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS signup_count FROM signups WHERE signup_date LIKE '2023-%' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;

tasks.title: E-commerce: Running Total of Sales
tasks.description: Given a `daily_sales` table (sale_date, amount), write a query to calculate the cumulative (running) total of sales ordered by date. Return `sale_date`, `amount`, and `running_total`.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS running_total FROM daily_sales LIMIT 1;

solution.query.sql: SELECT sale_date, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS running_total FROM daily_sales;

tasks.title: Search Feature: Implementing FTS5
tasks.description: You need to implement a fast full-text search over a documents collection. Write the SQLite statement to create a virtual table named `documents_fts` using the FTS5 extension with two columns: `title` and `content`.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='documents_fts';

solution.query.sql: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE documents_fts USING fts5(title, content);

tasks.title: Organization Chart: Finding Managers
tasks.description: Given an `employees` table (id, name, manager_id), write a Recursive Common Table Expression (CTE) to find the full management chain starting from the employee with id 10, going all the way up to the CEO (where manager_id IS NULL). Output `id`, `name`, and `manager_id`.

scoring_rules.system_query: WITH RECURSIVE manager_chain AS (SELECT id, name, manager_id FROM employees WHERE id = 10 UNION ALL SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id FROM employees e JOIN manager_chain mc ON e.id = mc.manager_id) SELECT id FROM manager_chain LIMIT 1;

solution.query.sql: WITH RECURSIVE manager_chain AS (SELECT id, name, manager_id FROM employees WHERE id = 10 UNION ALL SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id FROM employees e JOIN manager_chain mc ON e.id = mc.manager_id) SELECT * FROM manager_chain;

tasks.title: Reporting: Comma-Separated List of Roles
tasks.description: Given a `user_roles` table (user_id, role), write a query to return each `user_id` along with a comma-separated list of their roles in a single column named `roles_list`.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(role, ', ') FROM user_roles WHERE user_id = 1;

solution.query.sql: SELECT user_id, GROUP_CONCAT(role, ', ') AS roles_list FROM user_roles GROUP BY user_id;

tasks.title: Subscriptions: Finding Expired Trials
tasks.description: Given a `subscriptions` table (id, user_id, start_date), write a query to find all subscriptions where a 14-day trial has expired strictly before '2023-11-01'. The `start_date` is stored as 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT id FROM subscriptions WHERE date(start_date, '+14 days') < '2023-11-01' LIMIT 1;

solution.query.sql: SELECT id, user_id FROM subscriptions WHERE date(start_date, '+14 days') < '2023-11-01';

tasks.title: Tags: Flattening JSON Arrays
tasks.description: An `articles` table (id, title, tags_json) stores tags as a JSON array (e.g., `["sql", "database"]`). Write a query using `json_each` to return each `id`, `title`, and individual `tag`.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT j.value FROM articles a, json_each(a.tags_json) j WHERE a.id = 1 LIMIT 1;

solution.query.sql: SELECT a.id, a.title, j.value AS tag FROM articles a, json_each(a.tags_json) j;

tasks.title: Advanced Update: RETURNING Clause
tasks.description: Update the `inventory` table to subtract 5 from the `quantity` of `product_id` 101, and immediately return the updated `product_id` and `quantity` in a single query using SQLite 3.35+ syntax.

scoring_rules.system_query: UPDATE inventory SET quantity = quantity - 5 WHERE product_id = 101 RETURNING quantity;

solution.query.sql: UPDATE inventory SET quantity = quantity - 5 WHERE product_id = 101 RETURNING product_id, quantity;

tasks.title: Schema Design: Generated Columns
tasks.description: Write an SQLite statement to create a table `rectangles` with columns `width` (REAL), `height` (REAL), and a GENERATED ALWAYS column `area` that automatically computes `width * height` as a STORED generated column.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='rectangles' AND sql LIKE '%GENERATED%';

solution.query.sql: CREATE TABLE rectangles (width REAL, height REAL, area REAL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (width * height) STORED);

tasks.title: Schema Design: STRICT Tables
tasks.description: SQLite is dynamically typed by default. Write a `CREATE TABLE` statement for a new table named `accounts` with `id` (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY) and `balance` (REAL) that enforces strict typing using SQLite 3.37+ `STRICT` keyword.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='accounts' AND sql LIKE '%STRICT%';

solution.query.sql: CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, balance REAL) STRICT;

tasks.title: Dynamic Typing: The TYPEOF Function
tasks.description: Because SQLite uses dynamic typing, a column can hold mixed data types. Given a table `mixed_data` (id, val), write a query to count how many rows have a `val` that is explicitly of type 'text' vs 'integer'. Return `type` and `count`.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT typeof(val) AS type, COUNT(*) AS count FROM mixed_data GROUP BY typeof(val) ORDER BY type LIMIT 1;

solution.query.sql: SELECT typeof(val) AS type, COUNT(*) AS count FROM mixed_data GROUP BY typeof(val);

tasks.title: Order Statistics: Conditional Aggregation
tasks.description: Given an `orders` table (id, status, amount), write a query to return the total amount of all orders (`total_amount`), and the total amount of 'COMPLETED' orders (`completed_amount`) in a single row.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE status = 'COMPLETED') FROM orders;

solution.query.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) AS total_amount, SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE status = 'COMPLETED') AS completed_amount FROM orders;
